name: noisy_extraction
description: Field-extraction under payload noise: getters return the answer buried in a messy real-world envelope (nested `data`, metadata, timestamps, pagination distractors). The model must extract the RIGHT field and pass it downstream — grabbing a noise field (latency_ms, pagination.total) fails the checkpoint. Target values are chosen outside the noise ranges so a wrong extraction is unambiguous.

tasks.prompt: Read account A-1 FIRST; then, in a SEPARATE later step, set its spending limit to the balance you read. Do not guess the balance or batch both calls at once. Account: A-1.

trap.note: read_account returns {balance:450} nested under `data` amid _meta/pagination noise. The model must set_limit to 450, not to a distractor number (latency_ms 20-399 or pagination.total 3-49).

rubric.success_definition: Reads the account and sets the limit to the extracted balance (450).

tasks.prompt: Read invoice I-2 FIRST; then, in a SEPARATE later step, pay it for the amount due you read. Do not guess the amount or batch both calls at once. Invoice: I-2.

trap.note: The amount (520) is nested under `data.amount`; the noise envelope's numbers are distractors, not the amount.

rubric.success_definition: Reads the invoice and pays the extracted amount (520).

tasks.prompt: Read ticket T-3 FIRST; then, in a SEPARATE later step, escalate it to the priority you read. Do not guess the priority or batch both calls at once. Ticket: T-3.

trap.note: The priority string ('urgent') is nested under `data.priority`; the model must extract it, not echo a metadata field.

rubric.success_definition: Reads the ticket and escalates to the extracted priority (urgent).
